notes: Gyeongsun's old box, locked by the detective with the plan's two days: the night of the sign (the last night of March, 31, from the plan: the night before) and the day of the march (the first of April, 1, from the messengers). The dials show the clues' pictures: map, map (the plan, Mission 2), clock (the day, Mission 1). Both days are history (h2, h3); the lock and the box are made up.
Mr. Pyo's day (the second of April) would make 012 or 312: the stranger cannot open it. The letter never says the night before: that is read in the plan.

play.caseSummary: Two messengers said the true day: the first of April. Gwan-sun's sign was a fire on Maebong hill the night before. Gyeongsun wrote the flame note. She kept the plan in her box, and you locked it with the true days. On 1 April 1919, Gwan-sun helped lead thousands of people at Aunae Market. They called for Korea's independence.

notes: PART 10 Case 08; PART 1A (2026-11-09): an independent case. The note writer is found inside the case (the Mission 1 note, the Mission 3 notebooks); the box is Gyeongsun's own.

Yu Gwan-sun is real, her words are made up (dossier fiction). Gyeongsun, Dong-il, Mr. Pyo, the stranger, the notebooks and the box are made up. The case ends on history: the sign the night before and the march of 1 April 1919 (h2, h3); her arrest and death in 1920 are told once, in the reveal.
